chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is struck on his ear and some of his eyesight goes away: what is to be given for that?

He said: "One of them is covered, then an egg is placed for him, then he is told: 'Look.' As long as he claims that he can see its place, until when one reaches a point that, if it is passed, he says, 'I do not see,' it is brought nearer to him until he sees. Then that place is marked. Then that is measured from behind him, from his right, and from his left. If it comes out equal, otherwise it is said to him, 'You have lied,' until he tells the truth."
He said: I said, "Is he not to be trusted?" He said: "No, and no honor; and the other eye is dealt with in the same way, then that is measured against the diyah of the eye."

key_terms.الْعَيْنِ: the eye, whose full diyah is the basis for proportional calculation
key_terms.بَيْضَةٌ: an egg used here as a visual object for testing sight
key_terms.كَذَبْتَ: you have lied, said when the claimant's report is inconsistent
key_terms.يُعَلَّمُ: it is marked or identified precisely

ai.seo_question: How is compensation determined in Shia fiqh for partial loss of eyesight after an injury?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a method for assessing partial loss of eyesight caused by injury in order to determine compensation. It describes a practical procedure for testing the extent of vision loss and then calculating the indemnity proportionately against the diyah of the eye.
